title: 9.4 A 102ns/V 94.3%-Peak-Efficiency Symbol-Power-Tracking Supply Modulator for 5G NR Power Amplifiers
problem: 5G power amplifiers require symbol-level power tracking to match instantaneous transmit power, but achieving fast voltage transitions (102ns/V) within cyclic prefix duration (1.17µs) while maintaining efficiency remains challenging.
motivation: 5G NR systems demand dynamic supply modulation of RFPAs to improve efficiency, but traditional buck-boost and LDO approaches suffer from slow tracking speed, large passive components, and efficiency degradation during transients.
method: Symbol-power-tracking supply modulator using split-capacitor topology with direct switching converter and auxiliary circuits to achieve 102ns/V tracking speed and 94.3% dynamic efficiency within brief cyclic-prefix intervals.
key_novelty: Optimized split-capacitor charging architecture with pre-charging and dynamic efficiency management to achieve sub-microsecond voltage transitions required by 5G FR1 symbol periods.
contributions: Achieved 102ns/V tracking speed meeting FR1 cyclic-prefix constraints (1.17µs minimum)
94.3% peak efficiency during symbol power tracking
Eliminates need for large external capacitors and off-chip components
Supports minimum symbol durations down to ~1.17µs without degraded efficiency
baselines: MHz-range switching converters with large passive components
primary_theme: fast symbol-level power tracking for 5G RF amplifiers
